column1: fraudulent§The fraudulent claims went undetected for six years because nobody ever checked a receipt against a bank record.§这些**欺诈性的**报销六年未被发现，因为从没有人拿收据核对过银行记录。§fraud（欺骗，同 fraud 诈骗）
frisky§The frisky young horse threw its rider twice before lunch and stood perfectly still for the vet.§这匹**活蹦乱跳的**小马午饭前掀下骑手两次，见了兽医却站得纹丝不动。§
frivolity§The frivolity of the opening chapter is deliberate: the book turns very dark in its second half.§第一章的**轻浮**是刻意的——这本书的后半部分变得非常晦暗。§friv（琐碎）
frivolous§The court dismissed the suit as frivolous and ordered the plaintiff to pay both sides' costs.§法院以**无理取闹**为由驳回诉讼，并令原告承担双方的费用。§
frolicsome§A frolicsome puppy is charming for about a week and exhausting for the eighteen months that follow.§一只**嬉闹的**小狗迷人大约一周，此后十八个月让人筋疲力尽。§
frugal§Her frugal habits were formed in a year of genuine hardship and never once relaxed after it ended.§她**节俭的**习惯是在真正艰难的一年里形成的，此后从未松懈过。§frug（果实／价值）
frustration§The frustration is procedural: four forms, three offices, and a decision that takes about nine minutes.§这种**挫败感**是程序造成的——四张表、三个办公室，而决定本身约需九分钟。§frustr（徒劳）
fulsome§His fulsome praise embarrassed everyone, and the person praised left the room before he finished.§他**过分肉麻的**赞美让所有人尴尬，被赞美的人没等他说完就离场了。§full（充满）→ 满得发腻
funerary§The funerary objects were removed in 1904 and returned, after a ninety-year dispute, in 1996.§这些**丧葬用**器物于 1904 年被取走，在九十年的争议后于 1996 年归还。§funer（葬礼，同 funeral 葬礼）
furious§She was furious about the decision and precise about the reasons, which made her far harder to dismiss.§她对这个决定**极为愤怒**，而对理由说得精确，这让她难以被打发。§fur（狂怒）
futile§Four appeals proved futile, and the fifth succeeded only because a new document surfaced in an unrelated case.§四次上诉都**徒劳无功**，第五次成功只因一份新文件在一桩无关案件中浮出。§fut（倒出）→ 像漏水的瓶子，白费
futility§The futility of the exercise was clear to everyone doing it and invisible to everyone ordering it.§这项工作的**无谓**对做的人清清楚楚，对下令的人则毫无察觉。§
gaffe§The gaffe lasted nine seconds and dominated three days of coverage that no policy announcement ever received.§这次**失言**持续九秒，主导了三天的报道，任何政策发布都没得到过这种关注。§
gaiety§The gaiety of the first evening did not survive the news that arrived on the second.§第一晚的**欢快**没能挺过第二天传来的消息。§
gall§He had the gall to ask for a reference from the manager he had publicly accused of incompetence.§他竟有这种**厚脸皮**，向一位被他公开指责无能的经理索要推荐信。§
gallantry§The gallantry medal was awarded in 1945 and collected, by his daughter, sixty-one years later.§这枚**英勇**勋章 1945 年授予，六十一年后由他女儿领取。§
galvanize§The photograph galvanized a campaign that had spent two years failing to interest anyone at all.§这张照片**激励**了一场此前两年始终引不起任何人兴趣的运动。§Galvani（伽伐尼，电击使蛙腿抽动）
garner§She garnered support one department at a time, and by the vote she had already counted the majority.§她一个部门一个部门地**积攒**支持，到投票时她早已数出了多数票。§
garnish§The dish is garnished with a herb nobody eats, and removing it would save the kitchen an hour a night.§这道菜**装点**着一种没人吃的香草，去掉它每晚能给厨房省一小时。§
gaudy§The lobby is gaudy in a way that was expensive in 1988 and looks cheap in every photograph since.§这个大堂的**俗艳**在 1988 年是昂贵的，此后在每张照片里都显得廉价。§
generalize§It is tempting to generalize from four cases, and every one of the resulting claims has since collapsed.§从四个案例**一般化**很诱人，而由此得出的每一条论断此后都垮了。§gener（类，同 genus 属）
generic§The generic version costs a twentieth as much and is chemically indistinguishable from the branded one.§**通用名**版本价格只有二十分之一，化学上与品牌药无从分辨。§gener（类，同 general 一般的）
generosity§His generosity was real and unstrategic, which is why so many people were surprised by how little he left.§他的**慷慨**是真实而不讲策略的，所以那么多人惊讶于他留下的东西如此之少。§gener（出身高贵，同 gentle 温和的）
genial§The genial atmosphere of the seminar survived four years and one very serious disagreement about method.§研讨班**融洽的**气氛挺过了四年，以及一场关于方法的严重分歧。§gen（出生，同 genius 天才）→ 天生令人舒服
gentleness§Her gentleness with the patients was matched by a complete refusal to be gentle with the administration.§她对病人的**温和**，与她对行政部门毫不温和的态度恰成对照。§
geology§The geology of the site was known in 1958, and the tunnel was routed straight through the fault anyway.§这块地的**地质**情况 1958 年就已知晓，隧道还是径直穿过了那条断层。§geo（地，同 geography 地理）+ log（学问）
germinate§The seeds germinate only after a fire, which is why the species vanished from land people protected.§这些种子只在火灾后**发芽**，所以这个物种从人们保护的土地上消失了。§germ（芽，同 germ 胚芽）
gibe§His gibe about her fieldwork was repeated for years, and her fieldwork outlasted his entire theory.§他讥讽她田野工作的那句**嘲笑**被传了多年，而她的田野工作比他整套理论活得更久。§
glorify§The film glorifies a campaign that its own participants described, in letters, as pointless and badly led.§这部电影**美化**了一场战役，而其参与者在信中把它描述为毫无意义、指挥拙劣。§glor（荣耀，同 glory 光荣）
gluttonous§A gluttonous larva can eat four times its body weight in a day and then not feed again for a week.§一条**贪吃的**幼虫一天能吃下四倍体重的食物，然后一周不再进食。§glut（吞咽，同 glut 供过于求）
governmental§Governmental delay cost more than the project: by the time approval came, the contractor had gone bankrupt.§**政府的**拖延代价超过项目本身——批文下来时承包商已经破产。§
graceless§The apology was graceless and the compensation was generous, and only one of them was remembered.§道歉**毫无风度**而赔偿很慷慨，被记住的只有其中一样。§
gracious§Her gracious note to the person who had beaten her is the reason they later worked together for a decade.§她给击败自己的人写的那封**得体大方的**便条，是两人后来合作十年的原因。§grac（恩惠，同 grace 优雅）
grandiose§The plan was grandiose and unfunded: nine towers, a lake, and no commitment beyond the drawings.§这个计划**宏大**而无资金——九座塔楼、一片湖，除了图纸没有任何承诺。§grand（大）
grate§His constant corrections grate after about the fourth one, however accurate each of them happens to be.§他不停的纠正大约从第四次起就**令人烦躁**，无论每一次多么准确。§
gratify§It gratified her to be asked, and it gratified her more to be able to say no without consequences.§被邀请**令她愉悦**，而能够毫无后果地拒绝更令她愉悦。§grat（愉快，同 grateful 感激的）
gratuitous§The violence in the final act is gratuitous: nothing in the story requires it and nothing follows from it.§终幕的暴力是**多余无谓的**——故事里没有什么需要它，也没有什么由它而来。§grat（免费／恩惠）→ 白给的、没来由的
grimy§The grimy windows had not been cleaned since 1994, and washing them changed the whole room.§这些**污秽的**窗户自 1994 年起没擦过，洗干净后整个房间都变了。§
groundbreaking§The paper was groundbreaking and almost unread: it was cited eleven times in its first decade.§这篇论文**开创性**十足却几乎无人问津——头十年只被引用十一次。§ground（地面）+ break（破）→ 破土动工
gruff§His gruff manner hid an unusual patience, and the apprentices worked out the difference within a month.§他**粗声粗气的**做派掩藏着少见的耐心，学徒们一个月内就摸清了这个差别。§
guesswork§The estimate is guesswork dressed as arithmetic: four assumptions, none of them stated in the report.§这个估算是披着算术外衣的**猜测**——四个假设，报告里一个也没写明。§
guileless§Her guileless account of the meeting was more damaging than any accusation could have been.§她对那场会议**毫无心机的**叙述，比任何指控都更具杀伤力。§guile（诡计）+ less（无）
gullible§The scheme targeted the gullible and, when that ran out, moved on to people who simply trusted their bank.§这个骗局瞄准**易受骗的**人，等这些人用完了，就转向那些只是信任自己银行的人。§gull（欺骗，英语俚语）
hackneyed§The metaphor is hackneyed, and the essay would be sharper without the four paragraphs it takes up.§这个比喻**陈腐**，去掉它占用的四段文字，这篇文章会更锋利。§Hackney（伦敦地名，出租马）→ 被用滥了
hallmark§Precision is the hallmark of her work, and it is the one quality her imitators consistently fail to copy.§精确是她作品的**标志**，也是模仿者始终学不来的那项品质。§Goldsmiths' Hall（伦敦金匠会馆打的纯度印记）
hamper§Bad weather hampered the search for nine days, and the aircraft was found in an hour once the fog lifted.§恶劣天气**阻碍**了搜救九天，雾一散，飞机一小时内就找到了。§
haphazard§The filing was haphazard for forty years, and reconstructing the sequence took two people eleven months.§归档四十年来都是**杂乱无章的**，重建顺序花了两个人十一个月。§hap（运气，同 happen 发生）+ hazard（偶然）
hapless§The hapless official signed the form that four superiors had refused to sign, and only he was disciplined.§这位**倒霉的**官员签了四位上级都拒签的表格，最后只有他受了处分。§hap（运气）+ less（无）
harangue§The harangue lasted forty minutes and persuaded nobody who had not already agreed before it began.§这番**长篇训斥**持续四十分钟，没能说服任何在它开始前不曾同意的人。§
harass§Regulations meant to protect tenants are used to harass them, and the enforcement office has three staff.§本为保护租户的规定被用来**骚扰**他们，而执法办公室只有三名员工。§
harbinger§The first swallow is a harbinger of nothing in particular, though everyone in the village treats it otherwise.§第一只燕子并非任何事的**先兆**，尽管村里人人都不这么认为。§
harmonic§The harmonic structure is simple and the rhythm is not, which is why the piece is harder than it sounds.§**和声**结构简单而节奏不简单，所以这首曲子比听起来难。§harmon（和谐，同 harmony 和谐）
harmonious§The relationship was harmonious until money entered it, and then it lasted about six more weeks.§这段关系一直**和睦**，直到钱介入其中，此后大约又维持了六周。§
harmonize§The two accounts do not harmonize, and the difference is the whole subject of the inquiry.§两份说法**无法协调**，而这个差异正是整个调查的主题。§
harshly§The report judged her harshly for a decision that four other people had approved in writing.§这份报告对她的一个决定**严厉地**评判，而另外四个人曾书面批准过它。§
hasten§Nothing hastened the process, and the family waited eleven months for a certificate that takes two days to issue.§什么也没能**加快**这个流程，那家人为一份两天就能开出的证明等了十一个月。§hast（急，同 haste 匆忙）
haughty§His haughty dismissal of the objection was quoted at the inquiry, and the objection turned out to be correct.§他**傲慢地**驳回那条异议的话在调查中被引用，而那条异议后来证明是对的。§
hazardous§The route is hazardous in winter, and the council closes it for four months rather than maintain it.§这条路冬天**危险**，议会索性关闭它四个月而不去维护。§hazard（风险）
hedonistic§The hedonistic reading of the philosophy is the popular one and, on the evidence of the texts, plainly wrong.§这套哲学的**享乐主义**解读最流行，而依文本证据看显然是错的。§
heinous§The crime was heinous and the sentence was three years, and the disparity is what people remember.§罪行**令人发指**而刑期是三年，人们记住的正是这种落差。§
hesitant§She was hesitant for exactly one meeting and then argued the position better than anyone who had held it longer.§她**迟疑**的时间只有一次会议，此后把这个立场论证得比任何持之更久的人都好。§haes（黏住）→ 卡住不动
hesitation§A moment's hesitation cost the team the point, and the replay shows he was right to hesitate.§片刻的**犹豫**让球队丢了这一分，而回放显示他犹豫得有道理。§
heterogeneity§The heterogeneity of the sample makes the average meaningless and the subgroups genuinely interesting.§样本的**异质性**让平均值失去意义，也让各个子群真正有趣起来。§hetero（不同）+ gen（种类，同 genus 属）
hilarity§The hilarity in the back row was audible from the stage, and the speaker never learned what caused it.§后排的**哄笑**在台上都听得见，演讲者始终没弄清是什么引起的。§hilar（快活，同 exhilarate 使兴奋）
hindsight§Hindsight makes the decision look obvious, and the file shows that four options looked equally sensible then.§**事后诸葛**让这个决定显得理所当然，而卷宗显示当时四个选项看着一样合理。§hind（后）+ sight（看见）
historian§The historian who found the letters spent eleven years in an archive that four colleagues had called exhausted.§找到这些信件的**历史学家**在一座被四位同行称作已挖尽的档案馆里待了十一年。§
histrionic§His histrionic resignation speech was undermined by the fact that he had negotiated the terms for a month.§他**做作夸张的**辞职演说，被他已就条件谈判一个月这一事实拆穿了。§histrio（演员）
